Antagonistic pleiotropy theory suggests that certain genes beneficial for early-life reproduction may have harmful effects in later life, contributing to aging.  
If women who have more children tend to live longer, that contradicts the idea of a trade-off between reproduction and longevity, which is central to antagonistic pleiotropy.  
The other options either don’t directly challenge antagonistic pleiotropy or are unrelated to the reproduction–longevity trade-off.  

Final answer: (A)
